title: Hybrid kernel routing + threadpool partitioning to cut host syscall & copy noise
creator: Arielle Kim
description:
Summary: Investigate and implement a hybrid runtime routing layer that chooses optimized attention/kernel variants and scheduling strategies at request time, while reducing host-side noise (frequent syscalls, small memcpy bursts, and threadpool contention) that currently inflates tail latency during mixed-sequence workloads. Goal: reduce 99th-token latency on hosted API by 20% for mixed short/long workloads and cut CPU syscalls and memory-copy contention during prefill by 30% in lab benchmarks.

Background: Our profiling shows two recurring sources of unpredictable latency: (1) the runtime frequently issues many small syscalls and micro-memcpy operations when servicing concurrent prefill/decode flows (hot path: staging slab -> pinned buffer -> GPU upload), and (2) the host worker threadpool suffers contention when many concurrent requests schedule small kernel launches that have heterogeneous sequence lengths, causing poor cache locality and kernel warmup thrashing. Existing tickets optimized individual pieces (coalescing, prefetch, staging arenas). This ticket proposes a cross-cutting approach: adaptive kernel routing (choose kernel variant + buffering strategy based on request fingerprint) + host threadpool partitioning and syscall batching shim to reduce scheduling jitter and copy fanout.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end E2E benchmark (internal harness) shows >=15% reduction in 99th-token latency on mixed seq workloads compared to baseline v2026.02
Host CPU syscall rate (gettimeofday/ioctl/mmap/etc) reduced by >=25% under synthetic concurrency (200 rps, 50% short/50% long)
Memory copy events to GPU staging reduced by >=30% and consolidated into <4 bursts per request on average
No regression in throughput (tokens/sec) beyond 5% negative variance; ideally improve throughput
Changes gated behind a runtime feature flag and validated in canary cluster with rollout plan
progress_updates: 2026-03-11: Spike prototype completed for runtime kernel-hint metadata: request fingerprinting (seq_len, kv_hit_ratio_est, request_size_hint) added to scheduler layer. Microbench harness shows kernel variant selection can change per-request latency by up to 18% in isolation.

2026-03-12: Implemented syscall batching shim that aggregates small GPU buffer upload calls into a coalesced upload path for pinned staging buffers. Local tests show syscall count per request dropped ~40% in a single-proc loopback.

2026-03-13: Threadpool partitioning patch (NUMA-aware lanes + priority lanes for prefill vs decode) landed in branch ENG/564321-threadlane. Initial canary with 8 workers per lane reduces lock contention events by ~35% in perf flamegraphs.

2026-03-14: Integrated hybrid kernel router with threadpool patch. Running 24-hour soak on canary cluster (canary-3). Observed occasional regressions for very long sequences when fallback routing triggers; captured traces and added telemetry for kernel switch frequency.
decisions: Adopt hybrid routing: default to low-latency kernel for seq_len <= 128, switch to throughput-optimized kernel for seq_len >= 1024, and use an adaptive intermediate kernel for 128<seq_len<1024 depending on observed kv cache locality.
Implement a syscall-batching shim as a runtime library layer rather than kernel patching to keep deployment fast and reversible.
Threadpool partitioning will be NUMA-aware and expose per-deployment tuning knobs; default config will be conservative (2 prefill lanes, 1 decode lane per NUMA socket).
Expose feature flag 'hybrid_kernel_routing_v1' with telemetry: kernel_choice, reason_code, prefill_batch_id, threadlane_id, syscall_batch_size.
open_tasks: Write integration tests that validate zero-copy fallback semantics when DMA/pinned-buffers are unavailable
Add regression alerts in Console: token-latency-by-model and kernel-switch-frequency per-route
Benchmark across GPU families (A10G, A100, H100) to calibrate kernel thresholds and default routing table
Finalize rollout plan: canary -> half-fleet -> full with kill-switch and automated rollback criteria
Create ops runbook for troubleshooting kernel misrouting and memory pressure cases
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive kernel switching reduces per-request latency for mixed workloads but increases kernel cache churn and telemetry noise. We chose an adaptive thresholding approach to balance churn vs. wins.
If pinned buffer budgets are exhausted, syscall-batching shim falls back to existing per-chunk upload path to preserve correctness at the cost of higher latency.
This ticket coordinates closely with E2E teams: please advise if your routing/compatibility tests require additional hooks.
